To: [contact omitted] Meral Karan
got it. I actually get where she is coming from here. I think Georgia has done this well through their program. I am sure
there are others. But on the stocktaking and impact. Let's talk. I have an idea.
On Wed, Nov 9, 2022 at 1:00 PM Meral Karan <[contact omitted]> wrote:
We are working on the stocktaking as part of the Mission deep dives but it will inevitably be a work in progress. The
issue of what works is definitely nascent. I agree developing an evaluation would be helpful - I can talk with our
evidence and learning colleagues on what could be feasible. Also we're trying to get stronger on M&E to figure out how
to track improvements across programming.
A couple thoughts on her responses:
#1. She seems to want us to do more debunking and counter offensive messaging. I think this would be very
unpopular withmany Missions as many have told us that any counter offensive messaging just unleashes trolls at
unparalleled levels. I'm not saying it should never be done but I guess it would be good to better understand what
exactly she is suggesting here. If instead we're talking about positive affirmative messaging, we're definitely doing that
- although can definitely do more/better I'm sure.
2. Related to #1, her comment on #2 implies she thinks the example of the pilot in Kenya is our only effort in positive
messaging through social media. While I'm not sure we have always paid for advertising (as that appears sketchy and
less authentic) its clear from our discussions that USAID and the Embassy regularly have robust communications about
[opaque block] 10/22

our work including on food security. Definitely we can do more and better, no doubt. Its hard to quantify how many
positive messages we put out across all our Missions but its invariably a huge amount.
3. Her point on GEC - to be honest in our field discussions we have practically no missions really using the GEC data.
Either they don't find it relevant, don't get it frequently enough or - once again - can't really use it with partners nor with
our own public messaging.
Anyway, helpful to see her perspective on this.
Meral Karan
Team Lead, Democratic Resilience and Innovation Team
Center for Democracy, Human Rights, and Governance
US Agency for International Development
